body:
## Problem

The GH-1280 campaign supervisor had a "no new signal" stop: halt the run when N consecutive cases produce no new failure signature. It never fired. 2,302 of the 2,313 signatures in the long run were argparse `usage` lines, and argparse echoes the mutated tokens in its last stderr line (`error: unrecognized arguments: NaN`), so nearly every usage refusal looked new. The streak counter was 4 when the run ended.

The run was still bounded because it stopped at the 10,000-case mutation budget. But it is unproven that the run had stopped finding new behaviour when it ended. Codex's final QA qualified the acceptance criterion for this reason.

## Evidence

- `TESTS-RESULTS/2026-10-30+GH-1280/SUMMARY.md`, disposition D6
- `TESTS-RESULTS/2026-10-30+GH-1280/runs/long/supervisor-report.json` (`signatures`)
- Supervisor: `TESTS-RESULTS/2026-10-30+GH-1280/tools/supervisor.py` (`signature()`)
- PR #1283 (lands the evidence)

## Fix (campaign tooling only)

Give `usage`-class cases a signature built from the argparse error kind alone (for example `unrecognized arguments`, `invalid choice`, `expected one argument`, `required`), with the echoed tokens removed. Other classes keep their current signature.

## Acceptance

- Re-scoring the retained long-run telemetry (`runs/long/telemetry.jsonl.gz`) with the new signature gives a small, stable set of usage signatures (tens, not thousands).
- On that replayed stream, the no-new-signal streak reaches its configured limit before case 10,000, or the report states why it does not.
- No harness or production code changes.

## Why it matters

This is one of two prerequisites before a stateful `factory-primitive` campaign (see SUMMARY "Stop/go"). The other is the sandboxed `tick` failure (filed separately).
